lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.unitTitle: PF7 — Paying Taxes and Financial Plan Capstone
lessonRef.title: Unit assessment: record keeping and deadlines

objective: Learners quantify the financial cost of missing records by computing the tax effect of claimable and unclaimable expenses.
scenario: Tullia is an invented eighth grader completing a pretend assessment: $3,600.00 of invented deductible expenses across a simulated year, of which $900.00 has no supporting record. The invented tax rate is 22%. All figures are invented.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Compute how much of Tullia's invented expenses can actually be supported by records.

prompts.text: How much of the expenses is documented?

tasks.directions: Compute the invented 22% tax effect of the documented expenses and of the full amount, keeping both figures.

prompts.text: What is the tax effect of the documented expenses?
What would the tax effect have been with full records?

tasks.directions: Quantify what Tullia's missing records cost, and project the same failure across three simulated years.

prompts.text: What do the missing records cost this year?
What would the same failure cost across three years?

tasks.directions: The lost benefit was smaller than the expenses themselves.

prompts.text: Explain why Tullia's missing records cost $198.00 rather than $900.00, and design the minimum record-keeping habit that would prevent it.

remediation: If a learner reports the full expense as the loss, compute Tullia's two tax effects side by side and subtract before drawing any conclusion.
extension: Ask the learner what level of missing records would cost Tullia over $300.00 in a year, and to show the reasoning.
